near.question: how do communities govern a shared resource without privatising it
near.answer: Communities can effectively manage shared resources through commons-based peer production, where stakeholders collaboratively create and maintain the resource. This approach involves open contributory systems that allow for equal participation in governance and decision-making processes. By fostering participatory practices and ensuring transparent management, communities can prevent the overexploitation of resources and avoid privatization, as exemplified by Elinor Ostrom's work on governing commons.

full.question: how do communities govern a shared resource without privatising it
full.answer: Communities can govern a shared resource effectively by adhering to certain design principles outlined by Elinor Ostrom in her work on common pool resources. These principles include establishing clear boundaries, ensuring that those who use the resource monitor its condition, and implementing graduated sanctions for rule violations. Additionally, mechanisms must be in place for resolving conflicts among users, and decision-making processes should be controlled primarily by the individuals directly using the resource. By maintaining autonomy from external authorities while fostering internal cooperation, communities can manage shared resources sustainably without resorting to privatization.

render.title: Open Source
render.wikitext:
"'''A program is said to be open source if the full source code for the program is available publicly, with no constraints on how it can be used.''' That's it. We've looked at so many other possibilities, I've even discussed it publicly with Stallman, and he agrees that his philosophy is not open source, because there are constraints on what you can do with his code."

- Dave Winer [http://davenet.userland.com/2000/09/15/whatIsOpenSource]

'''On the necessity of open collaboration''':


" The free sharing of information - in this case code as opposed to software development - has nothing to do with altruism or a specific anti-authoritarian social vision. It is motivated by the fact that in a complex collaborative process, it is effectively impossible to differentiate between the "raw material" that goes into a creative process and the "product" that comes out. Even the greatest innovators stand on the shoulders of giants. All new creations are built on previous creations and themselves provide inspiration for future ones. The ability to freely use and refine those previous creations increases the possibilities for future creativity."
(http://news.openflows.org/article.pl?sid=02/04/23/1518208 )
